html:
The Albert Schweitzer Hospital is a hospital at Lambaréné on the Ogooué river in Gabon, founded in 1913 by Albert Schweitzer and his wife Helene Bresslau Schweitzer. It made Schweitzer one of the most famous people of the 20th century.

Schweitzer was already known in Europe as a theologian, an organist and a scholar of Bach. At thirty he began medical school so he could serve as a mission doctor in French Equatorial Africa. He started in a chicken coop. In the First World War the French held him as a German citizen; he came back in 1924 and built a larger hospital village, paid for with his organ concerts and lectures.

There he worked out his ethic of "reverence for life". He won the Nobel Peace Prize for 1952 and spoke out against nuclear weapons. Later critics found his hospital old-fashioned and his attitude to Africans paternalistic. The hospital carries on today, with a research centre on malaria and other tropical diseases.
